key_insight: UniMedSeg aims to unify multiple medical image segmentation paradigms—such as visual in-context, interactive, and language-guided segmentation—into one scalable framework. It also bridges 2D and 3D segmentation so a single model can learn from heterogeneous annotations and image types.
problem_solved: Existing medical segmentation foundation models are fragmented: different prompt paradigms and spatial dimensions are usually handled by separate models. This prevents joint learning from diverse annotations and limits generalization across clinical tasks.
method: Builds a unified in-context learning framework that can interpret multiple prompt types for segmentation.
Supports multi-paradigm segmentation, including visual, interactive, and language-guided inputs.
Extends the same modeling approach across both 2D and 3D medical images to enable shared learning.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reduces model fragmentation and simplifies training, deployment, and scaling across medical imaging tasks. It could make segmentation systems more flexible, data-efficient, and broadly applicable in real clinical workflows.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing different input paradigms flowing into one unified segmentation model
A split-panel comparison of 2D vs 3D medical image handling
Icons for prompt types: text, click/interaction, and visual example prompts
A before-vs-after graphic highlighting fragmented models versus unified learning
paper_title: UniMedSeg: Unified In-Context Learning for Multi-Paradigm 2D/3D Medical Image Segmentation
paper_authors: Yunzhou Li, Jiesi Hu, Yanwu Yang, Hanyang Peng, Chenfei Ye
